prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a site that (A) teaches crypto in plain English, (B) shows real numbers/transparent data, or (C) actually publishes the teacher’s own trade losses and mistakes? Those are three different things — I can point to a single source for one of them, but most people combine resources.

Short answer / quick recommendation if you want all three elements:
- Use a combination: Coin Bureau or Bankless for plain‑English explanations, Dune Analytics or Glassnode for “real numbers,” and Rekt.news/The Defiant for honest post‑mortems showing real losses and hacks.

Why that combo:
- Coin Bureau / Bankless — clear, beginner‑friendly explanations (videos and longform) that don’t assume deep technical knowledge.
- Dune Analytics / Glassnode / Nansen — dashboards and on‑chain data you can inspect yourself (actual transactions, volumes, fees, address balances). That’s “real numbers.”
- Rekt.news and The Defiant — catalog post‑mortems, hacks, exploits and protocol failures; they show what went wrong and how much was lost.

Other useful picks depending on what you meant:
- If you want a single plain‑English site with bite‑sized lessons: Coinbase Learn or Binance Academy.
- If you specifically want creators who publish their own P&L and losses: that’s rarer (and potentially regulated). Look for independent traders on YouTube/Twitter who post full trade journals (e.g., some crypto traders on Twitter or YouTube), but treat self‑reported P&L cautiously.
- If you want audited historical performance of strategies: look for institutional research (Messari, Kaiko) or on‑chain strategy dashboards on Dune where you can verify outcomes.

If you tell me which of A/B/C matters most to you (or if you want one consolidated resource vs. a compact reading list), I’ll give a tailored, ranked recommendation and specific links.
